### Observed differences

- The activities A19, A20 and A25 each appeared in essentially every trace in the earlier window (200 of 200) but in only about 53 in 100 traces in the later window (106–107 of 200), with no meaningful repetition per trace in either window. [OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]
- A41's routing changed: in the earlier window about 96 in 100 of its outgoing transitions led to A19, while in the later window about 50 in 100 lead to A19 and about 44 in 100 lead directly to A26, which was not observed as a successor of A41 before. [DIR005]
- Accordingly, the ordered pair A41 then A26, previously about 4 event positions apart in about 93 in 100 of its occurrences, is in the later window immediately adjacent in about 44 in 100 occurrences, while the 4-step gap remains in about 49 in 100. [LAG002]
- The internal order of the A19/A25/A20 group is preserved: A25 still leads to A20 in about 98 in 100 of its outgoing transitions and A20 still leads to A26 in about 96–99 in 100, in both windows. [DIR003, DIR004]
- A02 became much rarer and changed context: about 29 in 100 traces before versus about 9 in 100 after; when present it now sits around mid-trace by event position (mean about 0.51 versus about 0.90), and its outgoing transitions, formerly about 85 in 100 towards A47, are dispersed with no target above about 18 in 100; the after-window picture rests on only 17 traces. [OCC001, POS001, DIR001]
- A46 now leads almost always directly to A47 (about 96 in 100, up from about 75 in 100), the transition A46 then A02, previously about 25 in 100, has nearly disappeared, and the A46–A47 pair is now almost always adjacent. [DIR006, LAG003]
- Smaller, weakly supported shifts: A04 and A06 each appear in roughly 12 in 100 later-window traces versus 4–5 in 100 before (24 and 25 versus 9 and 8 traces), and A08's outgoing profile changed completely but rests on only 4 before and 15 after observations. [OCC002, OCC003, DIR002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

In the later window, the segment A19 → A25 → A20, which follows A41 and precedes A26, is bypassed in roughly half of the executions: A41, which previously led to A19 in about 96 in 100 cases and reached A26 only about four positions later, now leads directly to A26 in about 44 in 100 cases, while the segment still runs, in its previous order, in the roughly 53 in 100 traces where its activities appear. The signs agree quantitatively — the roughly 44 in 100 direct A41→A26 successions and immediate adjacencies match the roughly 47 in 100 traces that lost the segment — the key items rest on about 200 observations per window, and 19 control-flow items qualified against roughly 0.6 expected for an unchanged process, more than chance would produce. The evidence cannot show whether the bypassed traces follow one common route after A41 or several different ones, nor whether the segment is now skipped in whole or replaced by unobserved work, and the occurrence, direction and gap items partly describe the same underlying behaviour rather than independent confirmations. [OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, DIR005, LAG002, DIR003, DIR004]

Other differences: A02 nearly disappeared (about 29 in 100 traces down to about 9 in 100), and with it the former detour A46 → A02 → A47, so that A46 now proceeds directly to A47; when A02 does occur it appears at earlier event positions and with dispersed successors, though this rests on 17 after-window traces. A04 and A06 occur somewhat more often and A08 shows a changed outgoing profile, all based on few observations. [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, DIR006, LAG003, OCC002, OCC003, DIR002]
